141: ✦People may tell you, 'You're pregnant, you should eat for two.'✦Don't believe it, even if your appetite is big.✦In the first 6 months, about 300 extra calories a day is enough.✦With twins it may be 500–600 calories.✦In the last 3 months you can eat around 600–800 extra calories.✦With twins this may be more.✦In a normal pregnancy, going far beyond your needs isn't necessary and will come back as extra weight.
142: ✦This week, the placenta, which provides nutrients and oxygen to the baby, is expected to be at the level of the mid-abdomen.✦If it's low, there's a chance it will move up between weeks 24 and 32.✦If it's very low, this is called placenta praevia; if the placenta covers the birth canal, it prevents a vaginal birth.✦In that case a vaginal birth could cause heavy blood loss and complications.✦When the placenta is low, some mothers-to-be may bleed, mostly between weeks 34 and 38.✦In that case the doctor following the pregnancy must be informed.✦If the placenta doesn't block the birth canal, labour has started and there isn't heavy bleeding, a vaginal birth can happen.
143: ✦Even if you have a big appetite, don't believe you need to eat for two. In the first 6 months, about 300 extra calories a day is enough.✦With twins it may be 500–600 calories.✦In the last 3 months you can eat around 600–800 extra calories.
144: ✦This week the doctor checks sugar and protein in your urine and the height of the top of your uterus.
145: ✦Your varicose veins are more noticeable now.✦If they run in your family, you may be more prone to them.✦They may become more noticeable with age and with each pregnancy.✦To reduce them, exercise regularly and put your feet up to rest whenever you can.✦Wearing compression stockings and sleeping on your left side also helps.
146: ✦Changes in the mother this week include:✦White vaginal discharge,✦Pain in the lower belly,✦Constipation and leg cramps,✦Heartburn, indigestion and gas,✦Changes in skin colour on the belly and face,✦A faster heartbeat as blood volume increases,✦Headaches and feeling faint.
147: ✦You may see thin, reddish, web-like spider veins on your ankles, legs and face.✦They're not uncomfortable and fade after birth.
148: ✦Your varicose veins are more noticeable now.✦If they run in your family, you may be more prone to them.✦They may become more noticeable with age and with each pregnancy.✦To reduce them, exercise regularly and put your feet up to rest whenever you can.✦Wearing compression stockings and sleeping on your left side also helps.
149: ✦Vitamin C is still an important part of a balanced pregnancy diet.✦It plays a key role in forming the collagen your baby needs for bones, teeth, muscles and skin.
150: ✦Throughout pregnancy your body always needs extra fluid.✦It's needed to increase your blood volume, support the baby's circulation and keep the amniotic fluid at ideal levels.✦Aim to drink at least two litres of water a day.✦If this makes you get up at night to pee, drink more earlier in the day.
151: ✦Your skin is affected by pregnancy hormones.✦This causes clogged pores and pimples in some women.✦Squeezing or touching them makes it worse.✦Cleansing your skin regularly with gentle products your doctor recommends can ease the problem.
152: ✦Limit caffeinated drinks.✦If you had a coffee habit before pregnancy, keep it under control during pregnancy.✦Caffeine can reduce the absorption of vitamin C, calcium and iron.
153: ✦Your body shape is changing; as the weeks pass your skin stretches and is more sensitive than before. Use moisturisers regularly to prevent dryness and irritation.
154: ✦Avoid strong sun, or always use a high-protection sunscreen before going out.✦Choose gentle, natural soaps, fragrances and detergents.✦When choosing clothes, prefer natural fabrics like linen or cotton.
155: ✦Vitamin C stays important throughout pregnancy.✦It strengthens cells and keeps them healthy.✦It helps both digestion and the immune system work well.✦It's essential for collagen formation and helps absorb iron from food.
156: ✦Your uterus keeps rising toward the level of your belly button.✦As it expands, it's normal to feel an ache in your lower belly from the stretching ligaments that attach it.✦This week the fundal height (top of the uterus) is about 23 cm.✦As the uterus rises, the angle of your ribs changes.✦This can cause mild pain in your chest area.
157: ✦The chance of a urinary tract infection rises in the second trimester.✦If this happens, tell your doctor right away.✦You'll probably be given antibiotics.
158: ✦You may have noticed your feet and ankles are swollen.✦Your legs retain fluid because circulation is slower.✦Your changing body chemistry also plays a part.✦Don't worry – your body will get rid of the extra fluid after birth.
159: ✦Rest with your legs up whenever you can.✦Avoid standing or sitting for long periods.✦Stretch your legs from time to time during the day.✦Wear comfortable shoes and supportive socks.✦Exercise regularly and don't cut back on water, even if swelling bothers you.✦If you notice sudden, severe swelling of your legs, hands, face or eyes, contact your doctor immediately.
160: ✦Your back pain might be caused by your bra.✦It's worth getting a bra that fits your bigger breasts and supports them comfortably.✦If you're above a healthy weight, back pain may be worse.✦So if you tend to overeat, it's time to rein it in and eat only what you need.
161: ✦Choose your shoes carefully.✦High heels can worsen back pain.✦During pregnancy, flat, comfortable shoes are best.✦Try not to stand for long periods.✦Don't carry heavy shopping bags.✦Sit down gently and don't sit for too long.✦Try not to slouch when sitting or standing.✦When getting out of bed, roll onto your side first.✦Try to relax your lower back.✦Prenatal yoga is great for this.✦When driving, adjust the seat back to support your lower back.
162: ✦Although calcium needs don't increase much in pregnancy, your body absorbs more, so pay attention to your calcium intake.✦Calcium is very important for your baby's bones and teeth and for your muscles and nervous system.
163: ✦This week your uterus keeps rising to the level of your belly button.✦The fundal height is about 24 cm.✦As the uterus rises and the angle of your ribs changes, you may feel mild chest pain from now on.✦Pressure on the stomach and intestines can cause digestive problems.
164: ✦Your belly keeps growing, which causes back pain.✦Choose flat, comfortable shoes to ease your joints.✦Rest with your legs up whenever you can.
165: ✦Hormonal changes at this stage may show up as emotional ups and downs.✦You may feel lost in excitement, worry, fear or similar emotions.✦If you're struggling, share your worries with someone close or talk to friends who have children.✦Talking to more experienced mothers can be reassuring.
166: ✦Over the past few weeks, your uterus has moved above your belly button and is now about the size of a football.
167: ✦Many women have their glucose tested between this week and week 28.✦This test (GCT) measures blood sugar to check for gestational diabetes.✦Untreated diabetes can make the baby grow too big, which can make vaginal birth harder.✦It may even lead to a caesarean.✦That's why this test is especially important.
168: ✦If you feel numbness in your wrists and fingers, it may be carpal tunnel syndrome.✦This numbness is usually linked to repetitive movements.✦But in pregnant women it can also happen for other reasons.
169: ✦If it hasn't been done already, your doctor may ask for a glucose tolerance test between weeks 24 and 28.✦Today this test is part of routine care and done with the mother's consent.✦Mothers at higher risk of diabetes may have a 100 g glucose test (OGTT), and those at lower risk a 50 g glucose challenge test.✦For the 50 g test, it doesn't matter whether you've eaten.✦The test is very important for detecting gestational diabetes.✦Gestational diabetes can cause the baby to be born very large and create risks for both mother and baby.✦Mothers diagnosed with it are advised a diet that controls sugar intake and limits sugary foods.
170: ✦As your baby's hair grows, your hair is starting to look fuller too.✦You might think you have more hair.✦But actually it isn't increasing – it's just not falling out.✦Enjoy it while it lasts, because your hair will start shedding again after birth.
171: ✦Lying on your front or your back isn't recommended now.✦Lying on your back is not advised because it presses on the large vein returning blood to your heart.✦It can disrupt your circulation and lower your blood pressure.✦It can also lead to digestive problems, haemorrhoids and back pain.
172: ✦In pregnancy, sleeping on your side – especially the left side – is best.✦Lying on your left side sends more blood to the placenta and helps your digestive system work well.
173: ✦Putting a pillow between your legs will help you sleep more comfortably.✦If you're used to sleeping on your back, place one or more pillows behind you so you're tilted at about 45 degrees.✦But still on your left side… Make sure your weight isn't on your back but toward your left shoulder.
174: ✦For a restful night, don't eat too much in the evening.✦Limit fluids in the evening to avoid getting up to pee.✦Sleeping on a high pillow or a few stacked pillows can prevent reflux at night.
175: ✦Do prenatal yoga before bed.✦Meditating after yoga helps you sleep deeply and calmly.✦If you're not sensitive to milk, a warm glass of milk an hour before bed can help you fall into a deep sleep.✦If you are, a bowl of yogurt an hour before bed is an alternative.
176: ✦This week you may feel very tired.✦Your heavier, forward-growing belly and bigger breasts may cause back pain.✦If you've gained more weight than needed, back pain may be worse.✦If so, start managing your weight right away.✦Excess weight gain can also increase the risk of gestational diabetes and pre-eclampsia (high blood pressure).
177: ✦About 1 kg of the weight you've gained so far has gone into the baby's development.✦The rest is the increase in fat, blood and fluid in your body.
178: ✦This week your uterus keeps rising to the level of your belly button.✦The top of your uterus is about 26 cm high.✦As it rises, it's normal to feel pain in your chest area.
179: ✦From this week you may feel tingling and pins and needles in your hands and feet.✦This condition, carpal tunnel syndrome, happens when fluid building up in your body swells the tissue in your wrists.✦Prenatal yoga has exercises that help.✦If they don't help and the problem is severe, you can see a physiotherapist with your doctor's approval.
180: ✦Gestational diabetes affects about 5% of pregnant women and happens when the body doesn't use glucose efficiently.✦It's most common in the last three months of pregnancy.✦Your doctor will check for diabetes around week twenty-eight.
181: ✦Take calcium and magnesium supplements if your doctor approves and recommends them.✦Put your feet up during the day to help circulation in your legs.✦Try exercises that stretch your legs, especially prenatal yoga.
182: ✦In these weeks you may suddenly feel your belly tighten for no reason – no panic 🙂 These are normal uterine contractions called 'Braxton Hicks'.
183: ✦If you've followed a nutritious, balanced eating plan, by 26 weeks you'll have gained about 7.2 to 9.9 kg.✦Remember: if you started pregnancy at a normal weight, ending it with a total gain of 11–14 kg is ideal.
184: ✦Your uterus is about 7 cm above your belly button, and about 27 cm from the pubic bone to the top.
185: ✦Stimulated by progesterone, your lung capacity keeps expanding this month.✦This change lets your blood take in more oxygen and get rid of more carbon dioxide.✦As a result you may breathe faster and feel slightly short of breath.✦Breathing exercises during pregnancy will help with shortness of breath and much more.
